- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 80+), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture the magnitude of the correction.
- Mean reversion is under-predicted: model holds prices too high for too long after peaks, failing to reflect rapid downward drift.
- Forecast bias is often downward in the last 10–15 days of the 30-day window, suggesting model is not adjusting for seasonality or policy-driven downward pressure.
- Lagged corrections are common: model reacts to price drops with delayed downward adjustment, often missing the immediate 1–2 day correction.
- Model exhibits “overfitting to recent highs” — forecasts remain elevated even when true prices are falling sharply, especially after 20–30 days of high prices.
- Forecasts are too optimistic in the first 5 days, then too pessimistic in the last 5 days — suggesting model lacks calibration to short-term volatility.
